body:
Fixes #741.

Six files convert a stack pointer through `TX_POINTER_TO_ALIGN_TYPE_CONVERT` and
`TX_ALIGN_TYPE_TO_POINTER_CONVERT`. `common/inc/tx_api.h` defines both macros only in
the **non-MISRA** branch of its `#ifdef TX_MISRA_ENABLE`, so with that macro defined
the two names are undeclared and none of the six compiles.

**The four simulator ports**, in `_tx_thread_stack_build()`, unconditionally:

- `ports/linux/gnu`, `ports/win32/vs_2019`, `ports/win64/vs_2022`, `ports_smp/linux/gnu`

**Two kernel files**, in the thread create path, inside `#ifdef TX_ENABLE_STACK_CHECKING`:

- `common_smp/src/tx_thread_create.c`
- `common_modules/module_manager/src/txm_module_manager_thread_create.c`

## Reproduction

```
gcc -m32 -c -DTX_MISRA_ENABLE -I common/inc -I ports/linux/gnu/inc \
    ports/linux/gnu/src/tx_thread_stack_build.c -o /dev/null

gcc -c -DTX_MISRA_ENABLE -DTX_ENABLE_STACK_CHECKING \
    -I common_smp/inc -I ports_smp/linux/gnu/inc \
    common_smp/src/tx_thread_create.c -o /dev/null
```

Both report the two names as implicit declarations, followed by an `int` to pointer
assignment. The same commands without the define compile cleanly, and so do all six
after this change.

No build configuration under `test/tx/cmake` or `test/smp/cmake` defines
`TX_MISRA_ENABLE`, so CI never compiles anything in that mode.

## Why inline rather than the existing idiom

`common/src/tx_thread_create.c` handles the same conversion with an explicit `#ifdef`
that selects the `ULONG` pair under MISRA. That is **not** a model to copy. On every
port that widens `ALIGN_TYPE` past `ULONG` — the AArch64 Cortex-A family, RISC-V 64,
win64 and the Linux simulator on `__x86_64__`, all of which declare `ULONG` as
`unsigned int` and `ALIGN_TYPE` as `unsigned long long` — a pointer round-tripped
through the `ULONG` pair loses its top 32 bits. Measured on the Linux port at 64-bit:

```
sizeof(ULONG)=4 sizeof(ALIGN_TYPE)=8 sizeof(void*)=8
original=0x7f1234567890  after ULONG round trip=0x34567890  TRUNCATED
```

Writing the conversion inline is what the non-MISRA macros expand to, what the
surrounding code already does — including the lines this replaces — and gives one form
that is correct in both modes and at both widths.

## Deliberately not fixed here

**`common/src/tx_thread_create.c` truncates** under the same two defines, for the reason
above. It compiles, so it is a silent wrong-pointer rather than a build break, and it is
reported separately as #744 with its own fix. Keeping it out of this PR keeps a build
fix and a behaviour fix reviewable on their own.

**`txm_module_manager_thread_create.c` has a second, unrelated truncation** in the same
statement: it casts `new_stack_start` to `ULONG` before the alignment arithmetic, which
the other two copies do not. Left alone here for the same reason; noted in #744.

## Verification

- All six files compile with and without `TX_MISRA_ENABLE`.
- SMP regression suite 117/117.
- ThreadX regression suite builds and passes.
title: Fixed the simulator ports and thread create paths so they compile when TX_MISRA_ENABLE is defined
